comments.body_html: So this is how I understand how airdrops work. Basically, airdrops have a percent chance to drop within a time of about 5-15 minutes and a cooldown of about 2 minutes after that. If the airdrop is unsuccessful after that time than it will wait 10 minutes or so to try again. So, since its a percent chance it doesn’t always guarantee the number of airdrops that you set. If it is successful with the airdrop spawn than it will start another attempt for an airdrop again after the cooldown time. Hopefully that makes sense.

No aggro from other Scavs. However, they were patrolling like crazy and wouldn’t stay in one spot for more than 5 seconds, not sure if that’s from this mod or not, but it was really cool. One of them even flicked me off! D:

Have to test for auto-aggro on maps other than Factory with the betterSpawns option set to ‘true’. I’ll have to do it another time though.

EDIT 3: Okay, I tried the mod on Customs and found a Scav who was friendly to me at first and was roaming across the map briefly. I lingered around them at a short distance to see how they would react, but they didn’t see me as a hostile at all. It wasn’t until I walked up to them to the point of almost hugging them where they turned on me and insta-Head,Eyes’d me.

Judging by this behavior, it seems like each Scav enemy is being treated as the Boss of that particular level as Bosses tend to be friendly to Scavs (with the exception of Killa and Tagilla) but will turn hostile if you get too close to them. Of course on Factory, though, if each AI Scav is being treated like Tagilla, then they will turn hostile to you regardless of distance which is exactly the behavior I was seeing.

Hopefully this helps in some way, otherwise I cannot recommend having this mod enabled if you want to hop on your Scav at any point.

EDIT 4: I have another theory: I’ve noticed that teleporting enemies around the map after they spawn seems to deal damage to them to where they shout voice lines that pertain to being in severe pain/near death. Is it maybe possible that this damage that should be treated as “environmental/natural damage” is instead being attributed to damage being caused by the player making them turn hostile?

comments.author: Beardy
comments.body_html:
In the mod’s spawnWaves folder (SPTARKOV\user\mods\PreyToLive-BetterSpawnsPlus\data\spawnWaves) there is a json config file for each map’s spawn waves. You would make your “sptBear” and “sptUsec” spawns to have a Time value of -1. For example for Customs, this would spawn a normal difficulty BEAR pmc in a random zone at the start of the raid:

{ “BossName”: “sptBear”, “BossChance”: 100, “BossZone”: “ZoneBrige,ZoneBlockPost,ZoneCrossRoad,ZoneCustoms,ZoneDormitory,ZoneGasStation,ZoneFactoryCenter,ZoneFactorySide,ZoneOldAZS,ZoneScavBase,ZoneTankSquare,ZoneWade”, “BossPlayer”: true, “BossDifficult”: “normal”, “BossEscortType”: “sptBear”, “BossEscortDifficult”: “normal”, “BossEscortAmount”: “0”, “Time”: -1, “Supports”: null, “TriggerId”: “”, “TriggerName”: “”, “Delay”: 0, “RandomTimeSpawn”: false }, This would spawn a normal difficulty trio of USEC pmcs in Dorms at raid start:

{ “BossName”: “sptUsec”, “BossChance”: 100, “BossZone”: “ZoneDormitory”, “BossPlayer”: true, “BossDifficult”: “normal”, “BossEscortType”: “sptUsec”, “BossEscortDifficult”: “normal”, “BossEscortAmount”: “2”, “Time”: -1, “Supports”: null, “TriggerId”: “”, “TriggerName”: “”, “Delay”: 0, “RandomTimeSpawn”: false }, I typically split the initial spawns up randomly between 3-4 zones with some overlap between USEC and BEAR pmcs, so the spawns are spread out and it doesn’t randomly choose to spawn them all in one spot (which could happen, however unlikely, if you included all spawn zones as an option). I do the same for a couple of SCAV waves at the start, then increment SCAV spawns out over the duration of the raid.

The Time value is in seconds, so if you do something like this:

{ “BossName”: “assault”, “BossChance”: 100, “BossZone”: “ZoneBrige,ZoneBlockPost,ZoneCrossRoad,ZoneCustoms,ZoneDormitory,ZoneGasStation,ZoneFactoryCenter,ZoneFactorySide,ZoneOldAZS,ZoneScavBase,ZoneTankSquare,ZoneWade”, “BossPlayer”: false, “BossDifficult”: “normal”, “BossEscortType”: “assault”, “BossEscortDifficult”: “normal”, “BossEscortAmount”: “0,0,0,0,1,1,1,2”, “Time”: 900, “Supports”: null, “TriggerId”: “”, “TriggerName”: “”, “Delay”: 0, “RandomTimeSpawn”: false }, There is a 100% chance a wave of 1-2 normal difficulty scavs (small chance for a group 3) will spawn somewhere on the map 15 minutes into the raid.

You can do random spawn times too. I tested this with the sniper scavs. For example:

{ “BossName”: “marksman”, “BossChance”: 33, “BossZone”: “ZoneSnipeTower”, “BossPlayer”: false, “BossDifficult”: “hard”, “BossEscortType”: “marksman”, “BossEscortDifficult”: “normal”, “BossEscortAmount”: “0”, “Time”: -1, “Supports”: null, “TriggerId”: “”, “TriggerName”: “”, “Delay”: 180, “RandomTimeSpawn”: true }, The above will have a 33% chance to spawn a hard difficulty sniper scav on the tower at some point during the raid (but not until at least 3 minutes have passed). The time range is controlled by the values entered in the default location base.json config files of SPT (SPTARKOV\Aki_Data\Server\database\locations).

Here’s how I have Customs (also known as bigmap) set:

“BotStart”: 0, “BotStop”: 2100, 2100 is 35 minutes into the raid. So on Customs between 3 - 35 minutes is when I have my sniper scav spawn chances (one for each sniper zone), always a surprise.

You can do the same with the BossWaves config files for each map if you want to change boss location or spawn chance.

It’s been super fun to tweak things so far. Raids have been awesome for me. Hope that helps!

}

Cheers!

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
I’ve already answered this about tagilla before so I’ll leave the post here:

“All bosses spawn instantly at raid start with the exception of tagilla on factory. There is no way to change this for tagilla without messing up the spawns. Since factory has only one spawn zone if tagilla spawns then no other ai is able to spawn until he dies. Any zone that a boss spawns in prevents other ai from also spawning in that same zone. So to make raids not completely empty on factory at the start of a raid i intentionally made him spawn in about 9 minutes after other ai has already got the chance to spawn in. Hope that makes sense. You can change the spawn chance in the config if you need to kill him for quests or want to guarantee he shows up in your raid.”

So having the ai spawn times all set to -1 is most likely causing them to not all be able to spawn. I understand what you want with having all pmcs spawning at the same time at raid start. But the whole purpose of the mod was to prevent this from happening and to also prevent them from spawn killing each other since their are only about three to four seperate spawn locations in factorys common openzone “BotZone”. Spacing out the time that each ai spawns allows the ai time to move away from the spawn locations and ensures they all spawn. Factory can only have 4-6 players in live tarkov. So, I made it have at least 5 pmcs spawn within the first 10 minutes, with a maximum of 15 to 30 pmcs over a 45 minute time span.

Hope that makes sense to you.

“All bosses spawn instantly at raid start with the exception of tagilla on factory. There is no way to change this for tagilla without messing up the spawns. comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
Hi donharkness,

Here are some examples of how to make the preset with 50/50 pmc spawns, all bosses, rogues, and cultists.

In the example, Bosses V1, all the bosses have a 5% chance to spawn. Since there are 8 bosses you will need to include 8 waves and the time they all spawn at. Which in this example I made them spawn 15 seconds into raid start. If you don’t want all of them to spawn exactly at 15 seconds then you can use the spawn delay to randomize the initial spawn. It works by generating a random number between the min/max for each boss and adds it to the 15 seconds. Setting any of the open zones to 1 means that that spawn zone can only be spawned in one time. This way spawns are spread evenly across the entire map. Once all open zones that you have selected have been used then it will reset and continue through them again. So, if you want the bosses to spawn in the same open zones and not seperated evenly then you will need to increase the weight of each zone to something like 2 or 3. All bosses will spawn with their followers. So for example Knight will also spawn with BigPipe and BirdEye.

The configPresetManager should look like the following:

Then, just make sure the name of the file you create is typed into the configPresetManager like:

Also fyi, the preset you create must stay in the preset folder.

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
The weight of each preset can be changed from 1-5. The higher the number the more often that preset will be chosen. Setting them to 0 disables them. Each map has separately made spawn presets. If you haven’t added any of your own spawn presets to the config then its best to just leave the default “PTL_BSP_MAIN_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV” presets to 1. With only the default presets, setting them all to 5 is unecessary to do unless you have other presets you have added that you want the mod to choose more frequently.

With the default settings you will 100% always have the “like-live-tarkov” presets be chosen. Either from the main spawn system or from the spawn generator. If the mod chooses a preset from the main spawn system then it will also attempt to choose a spawn generator preset that has the “enableMainPresets” option enabled. Which I titled these as “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_ADDON” within the config. If the mod chooses the “like-live-tarkov” spawn generator preset then it will disable the main spawn system preset.

It works like this.

Say for the map Customs you have only two presets: ’ “PRESET_A”: 1 ’ and ’ “PRESET_B”: 5 ’.

An array will fill as such: [PRESET_A,PRESET_B,PRESET_B,PRESET_B,PRESET_B,PRESET_B].

One of the presets in this array will be chosen by random. Since there are 5 of the PRESET_B in the array it will have a much higher chance/probability of being picked from the array.

Hope that helps you visualize what the weight system is a bit more and see why it would be unecessary to make all of them the same value of 5.

Also, changing the raid times back to default won’t mess anything up.

comments.author: TheDasta
comments.body_html:
I can help answer some of these for you.

Bot level relative to player means they will be in a range above or below your level by that amount. So 15 at level 5 means AI will be anywhere from level 1 to 20. If you’re level 30, then the range would be anything from 15 to 45. (This only seems to apply to 1 bot per wave though, so if one of your waves has 2 bots spawning together, then the first bot falls into that range, and the second one appears to be a random level).

The first option means that you aren’t limited to the extracts depending on where you spawn (ie, if you spawn at Emercom on Interchange, you’ll be able to extract at Emercom as well). The second option means that all CHANCE extractions are always available (Car extracts, for example, will always be available, or gas station on Customs).

You’ll want to configure this under your “main” or “spawnGenerator” json files. So below, it’ll spawn “easy” difficulty scav bots more than “normal” difficulty scav bots. The same configuration can be done for PMCs as well. This uses the weight system so 5 (most likely) all the way to 1 (less likely) and 0 = difficulty disabled so no “hard” or “impossible” difficulty bots will spawn.

Example of a json file:

PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV.json

“scavs”: {
“enabled”: true,
“botDifficulty”: {
“easy”: 5,
“normal”: 1,
“hard”: 0,
“impossible”: 0

For what it’s worth, I only use the “spawnGenerator” to control the bots. I find it easier.

Below is a snippet of my presets json file I use and you can see “main” is set to false and “spawnGenerator” is set to true with “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV” the only config file with a weight value.

“customs”: {
“extendedLogs”: false,
“main”: {

comments.author: Hustleharder
comments.body_html:
In config, you can choose the config you want to use. By default it’s spawnchangesonly. So, you go into the presets folder and select the preset you are using. In the preset, you can find a min and max for bots alive at one time.

However, changing the PMC ratios is a different story. Here’s what I did/am currently doing:

1. In the config/preset/spawnchangesonly I disabled spawnGenerators (ends up being more files to edit, but if you can be bothered, feel free to leave enabled)

2. in db/locations find the location you want to edit (Interchange) and go into interchange/main/presets

3. There are two presets, Like_live 1 & 2. You will need to edit both of them since each raid is a 50/50 on which preset is used.

4. Find “pmcs”: [ and edit the “BossChance”: value to be lower. By adjusting this, you can change the percentage chance for a PMC to spawn at the given time.

I typically leave start of raid times (0-1000) at 65% and drastically decrease the later times (1000-3000) so PMCs are less likely to spawn throughout the raid. This helps save performance (less PMCs fighting scavs) and makes it so interchange isn’t a total war zone. For Like_Live 2 I usually slightly decrease the starting spawn rates and decrease the later spawn times to a slightly higher value than Like_Live 1.

Hope this helps, best of luck!

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
The “initial” section allows you to set the amount of waves that will spawn at the set time. So in your example above there will be a total of 10 waves that spawn at the set time of 40 seconds.

The “interval” section allows you to set the amount of waves and the interval of time that they spawn at after the “initial” time. In your example above you have the time set to 500 seconds which is about equal to 8 minutes and your “wavesPerInterval” is set to 6. So every 8 minutes there will be 6 waves (in theory 6 waves will spawn, however remember that each wave has a spawn chance attached to it) out of the total waves possible, which you have set to 36. The total “waves” divided by the “wavesPerInterval” is how many times this can occur throughout a single raid (from your example: 36 waves / 6 wavesPerInterval = 6 total intervals). And to determine the amount of time until the ai completely stops spawning in the raid just multiply the total intervals by the time you set (so 6 intervals x 8 minutes = 48 minutes).

To have waves every 3 minutes just set the “interval” time to 180.

Sorry it is kind of a lot of math but hopefully it makes a little more sense to you now. Please let me know if you have any other questions.

“bosses”: { “enabled”: true, “botType”: { “glukhar”: 1, “killa”: 1, “knight”: 1, “reshala”: 1, “sanitar”: 1, “shturman”: 1, “tagilla”: 1, “zryachiy”: 1 }, “botDifficulty”: { “easy”: 0, “normal”: 1, “hard”: 0, “impossible”: 0 }, “botChance”: { “min”: 100, “max”: 100 }, “spawnWaves”: { “initial”: { “waves”: 1, “time”: 0 }, “interval”: { “waves”: 0, “wavesPerInterval”: 0, “time”: 0 }, “spawnDelay”: { “min”: 0, “max”: 0 } }, “onlyVanillaOpenZones”: false, “openZones”: { “ZoneBlockPost”: 1, “ZoneBlockPostSniper”: 0, “ZoneBrige”: 1, “ZoneCrossRoad”: 1, “ZoneCustoms”: 1, “ZoneDormitory”: 1, “ZoneFactoryCenter”: 1, “ZoneFactorySide”: 1, “ZoneGasStation”: 1, “ZoneOldAZS”: 1, “ZoneScavBase”: 1, “ZoneSnipeBrige”: 0, “ZoneSnipeFactory”: 0, “ZoneSnipeTower”: 0, “ZoneTankSquare”: 1, “ZoneWade”: 1 } },

If you are using the “spawnGenerator” method of spawn waves then here is an example for spawning any boss on Customs.

  1. Make sure to enable bosses.
  2. Select the type of boss wave you want to have spawn. In the example I chose a weight of 1 for each boss type which means each boss has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being picked. The weight system can only be 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.
  3. Select the difficulty that you want the boss wave to spawn with. In the example I just chose a weight of 1 for “normal” difficulty.
  4. Set the minimum and maximum chance that the boss will spawn. The mod will generate a new random number between the minimum and maximum for each new wave. In the example I set the minimum and maximum to 100 so a boss wave is always guaranteed to spawn.
  5. Set the number of boss waves you want to have spawn at raid start. In the example I made it so only 1 boss wave will spawn and I set a time of 0 which will guarantee it spawns as soon as a raid starts.
  6. Use “interval” waves only if you want the bosses to spawn at different time throughout a raid. The “waves” option sets the total waves that can be spawned into a raid. The “wavesPerInterval” option determines how many waves will spawn from the total waves. The “time” option sets the time that each set of waves will spawn. For example: a total “waves” of 30, a “wavesPerInterval” of 3, and a “time” of 240 will spawn 3 waves of AI every 4 minutes (240_secs / 60_secs = 4_mins) and will occur 10 times during a raid (30_waves / 3_wavesPerInterval = 10_times). This also means the AI waves will stop spawning after 40 minutes (4_mins*10_times = 40_mins).
  7. Use the “spawnDelay” to randomize the time for each wave that is generated. The mod will randomly choose a number between the minimum and maximum and apply it to the set “time” options in “spawnWaves” for each wave. (Can be a - or + number as well.)
  8. Select the open zones that you want the boss to spawn in. In the example I chose a weight of 1 for each zone that isn’t a “sniper” zone. Again this option uses the weight system which is 0-5. (Enabling the “onlyVanillaOpenZones” option will restrict the boss waves to only the “original” EFT spawn zones for bosses and it will also force only the “original” bosses to spawn in their “original” zones to keep it just like it is in EFT.)

Hope that helps.

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
The raid timer is just for setting how long a raid is and does not affect the time of spawn waves, hence why its also part of the “other options”. If you want longer raids that continue to populate with waves of bots then you will need to change the spawn presets (in “spawnGenerator” and “main” folders). The min/max values is used to randomize the time each raid. So, if you want a 1-2 hour long raid you can set the min to 60mins and max to 120mins and it will randomly choose a raid time between that range.

For really long raids (1.5hrs+) I recommend disabling the main presets within the config and using only the spawn generator presets since the main presets cannot be easily setup for longer raids. The main presets were all “handcrafted” by me and it takes a lot of time and testing to create them, but if you have that time and patience then go for it. This is the reason I created the spawn generator since it automates the process of creating waves for you.

Below is an example of what I would do for a 12 hour raid time on Customs using the spawn generator presets:

Lets say you want the waves of bots to spawn in an interval for 6 minutes for 12 hours. So,

Raid time: 12hrs = 720mins = 43,200secs

Interval spawn time: 6mins = 360secs

Total interval waves required: 43,200secs / 360secs = 120 interval waves

But now you need to decided how many waves of bots you want to have spawn per interval spawn time. Lets say you want 2 waves of bots every 6 minutes. So,

Number of waves required: 120 interval waves * 2 waves = 240 interval waves

Basically you will have to double the number of interval waves that will be required since 2 waves of bots will spawn every 6 minutes.

So, with this info, every 6 minutes you will have 2 waves of bots spawn (keep in mind the “botChance” plays a factor in whether or not those waves actually spawn in) and will occur 120 times in a 12hr long raid.

Below is what the JSON spawn generator preset would look like for PMCs with this info we just calculated:

“spawnWaves”: {
“initial”: {
“waves”: 10,
“time”: 15
},
“interval”: {
“waves”: 240,
“wavesPerInterval”: 2,
“time”: 360
},
“spawnDelay”: {
“min”: -90,
“max”: 90
}
},

I always start my raids on Customs with 10 PMCs hence why the initial waves is set to 10 and set to spawn 15 seconds after I load into the raid. Using the spawn delay you can randomize the spawn time of all waves. So all the initial waves have a time of 15 seconds but each wave will get randomized by adding a number between -90 and 90 to the 15 seconds. (Dont worry about something like 15secs + (-43secs) = -28secs happening and causing the number go negative. If it occurs then it will not get added to the 15 seconds.) If you don’t want randomized spawns and want everything to spawn at the exact same time then just set the min/max values to 0. The total interval waves is set to 240 and the waves per interval time is set to 2 as we calculated above. The spawn time for interval wave will also get randomized by the spawn delay, so that bots don’t spawn at exactly 6 minute (320 second) intervals.

Keep in mind that this will need to be done for every type of bot (pmc, scav, sniper, boss, raiders) on every map and each bot will be different. Meaning most likely you wouldn’t want bosses or snipers to use the same spawn interval as pmcs/scavs.

Hope that answers your question and helps you create a longer raid!

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
Here is how to have just a single “spawnGenerator” preset or “main” preset for every map.

1. Create a config preset or use an existing one. These can be found in ‘mods\PreyToLive-BetterSpawnsPlus\config\presets’. Make sure to type the name of the file you decide to use in the “configPresetManager” JSON file found in ‘mods\PreyToLive-BetterSpawnsPlus\config’, since this file determines what config preset is selected by the mod.

2. Either delete all the “main” and “spawnGenerator” preset key/value pairs in the config file you decide to use or set them all to zero.

*** Be careful though, if you just delete the “spawnGenerator” or “main” preset JSON files within the “locations” folder without also removing the preset name from the config preset then the mod will throw errors saying that it cannot find the presets. ***

4. Set either the “spawnGenerator” or “main” enabled option to false. Whichever you decide you do not want to use.

For example, change the config preset from this:

“customs”: { “extendedLogs”: false, “main”: { “enabled”: true, “enableBosses”: true, “presets”: { “PTL_BSP_MAIN_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV_1”: 1, “PTL_BSP_MAIN_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV_2”: 1 } }, “spawnGenerator”: { “enabled”: true, “presets”: { “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_ADDON_BOSSES”: 1, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_ADDON_CULTISTS”: 1, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_ADDON_RAIDERS”: 1, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_ADDON_ROGUES”: 1, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV_1”: 2, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV_2”: 2, “PTL_BSP_MSG_PRESET_MEETING_OF_THE_BOSSES”: 1 } } }, to this:

“customs”: { “extendedLogs”: false, “main”: { “enabled”: false, “enableBosses”: true, “presets”: { “PTL_BSP_MAIN_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV_1”: 0, “PTL_BSP_MAIN_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV_2”: 0 } }, “spawnGenerator”: { “enabled”: true, “presets”: { “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_ADDON_BOSSES”: 0, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_ADDON_CULTISTS”: 0, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_ADDON_RAIDERS”: 0, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_ADDON_ROGUES”: 0, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV_1”: 0, “PTL_BSP_SG_PRESET_LIKELIVETARKOV_2”: 0, “PTL_BSP_MSG_PRESET_MEETING_OF_THE_BOSSES”: 0 } } }, or this:

“customs”: { “extendedLogs”: false, “main”: { “enabled”: false, “enableBosses”: true, “presets”: { } }, “spawnGenerator”: { “enabled”: true, “presets”: { } } }, Do this same thing for each map name in the config preset.

3. Now create your custom preset for each map. Each map will need a unique preset made for it since each map utilizes different spawn zones for bots.

4. Now update the config preset with the file name of the preset. Make sure the map name that the preset is under is the same as the physical location of the file.

For example, lets say you create a “spawnGenerator” preset JSON file for the map Customs called “myCustomsPreset” (without the quotes). You would edit your config file like this:

“customs”: { “extendedLogs”: false, “main”: { “enabled”: false, “enableBosses”: true, “presets”: { } }, “spawnGenerator”: { “enabled”: true, “presets”: { “myCustomsPreset”: 1 } } }, or just add it to the list of other presets that have been set to zero, if thats what you decided to do instead of deleting all the key/value pairs.

Hope that helps you. If you still need help with anything please let me know.

comments.body_html:
Hi there! To disable the goons you will need to edit the presets for the following locations: Customs, Shoreline, and Woods. Within the “db/locations/” folder you will find the folders for these 3 locations. Within these folders are the presets for the “main” and “spawnGenerator” spawn systems. In the “spawnGenerator” folder you will find 3 presets that look something like this: SG_PRESET_(MAPNAME)_LIKELIVETARKOV_(#). Within each of these presets set the “bosses/botType/knight” option to 0. This will disable the goons and make them unable to spawn in-raid for that preset.

Below is an example of a “spawnGenerator” preset from the Customs location with the goons disabled:

“bosses”: { “enabled”: true, “botType”: { “glukhar”: 0, “killa”: 0, “knight”: 0, “reshala”: 1, “sanitar”: 0, “shturman”: 0, “tagilla”: 0, “zryachiy”: 0 }, After doing that for each like-live preset in the “spawnGenerator” folder for each of the 3 maps you will also need to do the same for each of the “main” presets. There are a total of 2 main presets for each map. Within these presets look for the “BossName: bossKnight” key-value pair in the “bosses” array and set the “BossChance” value to 0. This will disable the goons.

Below is an example of a “main” preset from the Customs location with the goons disabled:

“bosses”: [ { “BossName”: “bossKnight”, “BossChance”: 0, “BossZone”: “ZoneScavBase”, “BossPlayer”: false, “BossDifficult”: “normal”, “BossEscortType”: “exUsec”, “BossEscortDifficult”: “normal”, “BossEscortAmount”: “2”, “Time”: -1, “Supports”: [ { “BossEscortType”: “followerBigPipe”, “BossEscortDifficult”: [ “normal” ], “BossEscortAmount”: “1” }, { “BossEscortType”: “followerBirdEye”, “BossEscortDifficult”: [ “normal” ], “BossEscortAmount”: “1” } ], “TriggerId”: “”, “TriggerName”: “”, “Delay”: 0, “RandomTimeSpawn”: true }, Again, sorry for the response delay and the rerouting from Reddit. comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
No worries. Glad you are asking.

The weight system is 0-5. Here is an example of how the mod uses this weight system:

For “pmcs” you have two options: “bear” and “usec”.

If “bear” has a weight of 1 and “usec” has a weight of 1 then there is a 50/50 chance the wave that gets generated will be either bear or usec.

However the mod works by putting each bot type into an array.

So if you have “bear” set to 3 and “usec” set to 1 then the array will look something like:

[bear,bear,bear,usec]

If you have multiple waves that spawn for pmcs then the mod will go through the array and randomly select one of the pmc bot types for each of the spawn waves.

After it selects a bot type it gets removed from the array. After selecting all of them from the array then the array is reset back to where it started and then it does it all over again for the remaining waves.

Example for 5 waves:

Array: [bear,bear,bear,usec]

Wave 1: selects bear

Array: [bear,bear,usec]

Wave 2: selects bear

Array: [bear,usec]

Wave 3: selects usec

Array: [bear]

Wave 4: selects bear

Array: [bear,bear,bear,usec] <- resets

Wave 5: selects usec

Array: [bear,bear,bear]

So to increase the odds of a certain bot type being chosen you need to increase the weight ratio.

You’re assumptions about the spawn generator preset percentage is sort of correct but remember that this weight ratio system is also used for choosing presets. So each preset gets put into an array and chosen by random and depending on the weight ratio you can make certain presets have a lower/higher probability of being selected.

Hope that makes sense.

comments.author: DoubleOhJavi
comments.body_html:
The preset manager is where you decide which file type to run from the presets folder.

The options of the spawn files available is what makes the difference. For example: if you open “only_spawn”changes“ and use the “customs” options, you will see in the presets that “main_preset_customs” are both set to 1 same as “sg_preset_customs_live”. Meaning they all have a equal chance to run/load that setup for your next raid. You will also see that the “sg_preset_customs_addon” are all set to 0, so all those additional setup files will not run so your raids will be a lot less random since it will only be based off the 5 files that have a 1 assigned to them.

If you open the “preytolives” file though, you will see that everything is set to 1 minus the “sg_preset_customs” files which are at a 5, meaning that there is a higher likely hood your raid will have one of these 3 file settings active for your raid BUT not guaranteed as it will be random out of all the available options, which in this case is every single file available.

Those file are the ones you can alter to your liking to keep it more random in your raids, if you set all of them to have the same value types then your raids are all goign to be as easy or hard as you set the SCAVs, Bosses and PMCs to be according to your liking. If you do random setups for each file then that’s where it really shines in letting you have a file where there is 0% bosses or PMCs to spawn if you set one up like that or possibly one where all SCAV and PMC are set to hard difficulty only.

Long explanation so hopefully its not too confusing but hope that helps a bit and gets your going in the right track as to what you want to do/get out of the mod.

comments.author: NotBen_2
comments.body_html:
Apologies,

My initial description was not entirely correct. Let me clarify:

On SPT without using any bot mods or behavior mods I’ve never experienced any RAM/VRAM leakage. It was only when I tried using SAIN and yours together would my RAM start around 10g and creep to 29-30g (Max of 32g) by end of raid and VRAM start at 5.5g and creep to 8g (Max of 8,192mbs). I had this happen multiple times and would have to extract early to avoid running out of VRAM and causing more issues.

I think it’s combination of both mods together and BSG code

What I consider BSG Logic:

Bots load in and get cached in RAM, and when killed the corpse locations and their loot pools persist throughout the entire raid thus requiring more RAM usage. More bots load in and the cycle continues. 3D rendering properties of the bots and their interactions with other bots require VRAM. Corpse LOD is also persistent throughout (always at 100% no matter the distance), requiring more VRAM. Think of this standard interaction of BSG code as Adding Marbles to a Jar.

The issue I see in regards to mod combination:

Using BSP to alter spawn waves, number of bots per spawn and number of waves creates a perpetual draw on CPU and GPU resources over time. Think of this as adding additional marbles to the jar, not quite overfilling but still getting there. Without the SAIN mod though, the bots still have standard interactions with limited navigation around the map, therefore limited in interaction with other bots and PMCs which means less CPU/GPU resource allocation. (Bots can’t die if they don’t interact with other bots)

When adding SAIN to the equation, creating the ability for bots to navigate around the map to specific navmesh waypoints, get into firefights with other bots plus new combat logic requires more resource allocation - RAM and VRAM. Think of the jar being filled with vibrating marbles that gyrate and bounce off one another. Eventually, adding more and more vibrating marbles to the jar will cause them to overflow from the jar.

The SWAG/Donuts mod attempts to limit the overflowing of these marbles by removing marbles at the bottom of the jar, aka despawning bots that are the furthest distance from player, thus limiting the amount of resources being requested from the system

Do you monitor resource allocation via Rivatuner? This is how I monitor all resources in my games and I consistently saw VRAM increases and RAM increases over time with this tool.

This is not meant to insult your mod by any means, this is only an attempt to highlight issues present with mod compatibility.

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
It seems like the issue being described isn’t directly a mod or mod compatibility issue but more so a bigger issue that already exists within the glorious realm of BSGs trash code.

Some solutions do exist to reduce the number of marbles in the jar. Here are my thoughts and suggestions:

  1. Your VRAM usage is normal. I have 16GB VRAM and it sits around 12GB after a 2+ hour raid on Customs. I wouldn’t worry about maxing out VRAM. Turn down the “Object LOD Quality” and “Overall Visibility” settings since these can impact VRAM.
  2. The self-cannibalistic RAM issue is something everyone has an issue with in EFT. It’s the result of bad optimization. I have 16GB and it sits around 10-12GB after an 2+ hour raid on Customs/Lighthouse. Some people swear up and down you need 32GB… but you really don’t. I just turn on RAM cleaner and call it a day. Oh and restarting your game after every couple of raids helps clear the RAM too.
  3. BSG happens to implement corpse LOD into Tarkov. I’ve tested it in the past and its not great but it is there. Also, I’m aware of other mods that despawn bots furthest away from the player but that doesn’t mean that 100% of the “despawned” bot related resources are no longer within memory.

So, yes, I agree that increasing the number of bots and their associated loot pools, bot logic, and lifetime existence with these mods will of course result in much higher resource demand from your CPU/GPU. However, I still have to disagree that the combination of BSP and SAIN is the leading cause of the avalanching memory leak like you are describing. The marbles analogy is great but you have to remember that these mods aren’t designed to fix the memory leaks associated with BSG’s code.

Also, fyi, Solarints SAIN mod doesn’t increase distance navmesh or alter bot waypoint navigation points. Those are handled by DrakyiaXYZ’s Waypoints mod.

There are some issues with setting the spawn wave timers (I’m using only spawn generators, without main presets):

1. The interval time is actually doubled. If you set it to 60, the wave will actually spawn every 120 seconds

2. The last initial wave will actually count as the first interval wave, so for instance setting only 1 initial wave and 2 interval waves will create 3 interval waves (all at doubled intervals too)

comments.body_html:
I looked at my code from v1.1.5 and I see now where I messed up in v2.0.0.

I just needed to change this:

randomTime = Math.max(0, randomTime + timeInterval);

to this:

randomTime = (randomTime + timeInterval < 0) ? 0 : randomTime;

The ‘timeInterval’ kept getting compounded into the ‘randomTime’ upon each interation. I guess thats what I get for trying to simplify code and being half asleep LOL.

Again, thanks for pointing out this error. I’ll have this updated asap on the mod page!

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
The latest version 2.0.2 should fix any issues with bots not spawning at correct times. The issue was the interval and initial time of spawn waves were being calculated incorrectly causing many of the waves to be pushed further back than they should have been. So, by the time your maximum bot count was reached in a raid the sniper scavs spawn times were skipped and would never be able to spawn in.

Also, bosses cause ALL other bots to not spawn in the same zone they are in. I’ve explained this many, many times thoughout this thread, but essentially bosses have priority in open zones and since Factory only has one open zone all other bots are blocked from spawning until the boss dies. To mitigate this issue, I intentionally have made Tagilla spawn several minutes later into a raid than he normally would so that other bots have a chance to spawn in so its not a completely empty raid with just Tagilla raoming around.

comments.body_html:
I have a lot of this information in the “Spawn Features” tab and in the README.md file, so please reference those for more in-depth explanations.

  1. To make bosses have 10% spawn chance the quickest/easiest way is to set them to 10 in the global overrides option in the settings manager file. You can set the spawn chance % for any bot type in the game within this setting.

Again, you will need to reference the “Spawn Features” tab or the README.md file, since it explains these options. I made majority of the presets have them be 1-to-1 so there should usually be an even amount of Bear and Usec pmcs in each raid.
  4. By default I made all LIKELIVETARKOV presets spawn all bot types in their usual locations as they would in EFT.

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
The preset manager should by default be using the “settings_LikeLiveTarkov” folder configs. If this is the case then go to the locations.json file and underneath “factory” should be a listing of all the “main” presets and “spawnGenerator” presets. The “presets” are exact names of files found in the “db/locations/‘map-name’/” folders. Setting the value of these from 0 to 5 will determine the probability of it being selected. Main presets will be more complex/time-consuming to create and spawn generator presets are faster/easier to create. If you don’t feel like going to in-depth with creating presets then I recommend turning off the “main” presets by setting “factory”->“main”->“enabled” to false. Leave the “spawnGenerator” settings as they are. Now head over to the “db/locations/‘factory’/spawnGenerator/presets” folder and look for the files named “SG_PRESET_FACTORY_LIKELIVETARKOV_1”, SG_PRESET_FACTORY_LIKELIVETARKOV_2, and SG_PRESET_FACTORY_LIKELIVETARKOV_3. In each file go to “factory”->“scavs”. The “initial”->“waves” and the “interval”->“waves” options sets the total number of waves that are allowed to spawn in each raid. The “botChance” option will be what determines if these waves of bots will spawn. The “botAmountPerSpawnWave” determines how many bots spawn per wave, etc, etc, etc (All this information is in the mod overview page and in the README.md).

If you want to reduce scav spawns then I recommend setting the values close to the following and adjust to your liking. Also, you can check the logs in the BetterSpawnsPlus mod folder to see what it generates before each raid, to determine if its a good balance of scavs/pmcs and to check if its working as you had intended. (please do not copy/paste the code below, may cause issues):

“scavs”: {
“enabled”: true,
“botDifficulty”: {
“easy”: 3,
“normal”: 5,
“hard”: 1,
“impossible”: 0
},
“botChance”: {
“min”: 65,
“max”: 75
},
“botAmountPerSpawnWave”: [1,1,1,1,1,1,1,2,2,2],
“spawnWaves”: {
“initial”: {
“waves”: 3,
“time”: 60
},
“interval”: {
“waves”: 12,
“wavesPerInterval”: 1,
“time”: 160
},

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
Essentially bosses have priority in open zones (areas that all bots spawn in and roam around in) and since Factory only has one open zone all other bots are blocked from spawning until the boss dies. To mitigate this issue, I intentionally have made Tagilla spawn several minutes later into a raid than he normally would so that other bots have a chance to spawn in and prevent it being a completely empty raid with just Tagilla roaming around. This is the only boss I’ve changed to be like this though and it is a work around I came up with since I don’t have much control of the bosses priorities. All other bosses on all other maps spawn on raid start just as they would in live Tarkov.

If you still would like to change this you will have to adjust his spawn time in all of the “spawnGenerator” and “main” presets for Factory. His spawn time on Factory is already set to be somewhere between 2-9 minutes depending on the preset that gets selected.

Setting a wider “interval” time will make the bots not spawn further apart and not so quickly after you clear an area. To clarify on how this works, you set the total pool of waves possible, then you set the total waves to spawn from that pool based on the time interval you have set. I provided a basic demonstration below that hopefully helps visualize how the spawns work.

* = spawn wave

Raid start - * * * * - 90 secs - * * * * - - - * - 510 secs - * - - - * - 930 secs - * - - - * - 1350secs - *

“initial”: {

“waves”: 8,

“time”: 90

“interval”: {

“waves”: 6,

“wavesPerInterval”: 2,

“time”: 420

“spawnDelay”: {

“min”: -30,

“max”: 30

From above, the raid starts with 8 initial waves that spawn at ~90secs, based on the delay that was set per wave. Then the interval waves start after the initial waves, hence why the first interval wave starts at 510secs (90secs + 420secs) and are also delayed based on your delay settings.

If you want overall less bots towards the end of a raid either make it so the interval waves run out by a certain time or adjust the “forceStopSpawnWaves” option found in the “settingsmanager.json”. From the example above, you can see the interval waves will run out after 1350 secs (22.5 minutes). This is one way to do it, and I believe is the best method. Using the “forceStopSpawnWaves” is a simpler solution but it basically removes any spawn waves that are generated with a spawn time over the time you have entered for the pmcs/scavs.

Hopefully that answers your questions and gets you closer to generating the spawns you want. If you still need help with anything please don’t hesitate to ask.

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
Yes your assumptions for the initial and interval spawn times and waves are correct.

The zone the bots spawn in depends on the weight distribution in the “openZones” setting. For example, say you have the weights distributed for PMC on Interchange as shown below.

“openZones”: {
“ZoneCenter”: 2,
“ZoneCenterBot”: 2,
“ZoneGoshan”: 2,
“ZoneIDEA”: 2,
“ZoneIDEAPark”: 1,
“ZoneOLI”: 2,
“ZoneOLIPark”: 1,
“ZonePowerStation”: 2,
“ZoneRoad”: 1,
“ZoneTrucks”: 1
}

The mod will store these “openZones” into an array as such:

[ZoneCenter,ZoneCenter,ZoneCenterBot,ZoneCenterBot,ZoneGoshan,ZoneGoshan,ZoneIDEA,ZoneIDEA,ZoneIDEAPark,ZoneOLI,ZoneOLI,ZoneOLIPark,ZonePowerStation,ZonePowerStation,ZoneRoad,ZoneTrucks]

When the mod begins generating PMC spawn waves for Interchange it first selects one random “openZone” from the array and then removes that “openZone” from the array. So if it selects ZoneGoshan for a PMC spawn then the array will now be:

[ZoneCenter,ZoneCenter,ZoneCenterBot,ZoneCenterBot,ZoneGoshan,ZoneIDEA,ZoneIDEA,ZoneIDEAPark,ZoneOLI,ZoneOLI,ZoneOLIPark,ZonePowerStation,ZonePowerStation,ZoneRoad,ZoneTrucks]

If the array is completely emptied of all its “openZones” and if their are still spawn waves to be generated, the mod will then refill the array back to how it started. It will continue to do this routine until all spawn waves for the PMCs have been generated. So if you want more bots in a certain area of the map I suggest increasing the weight of that “openZone” (the weight can only be 0-5).

Keep in mind the maximum bot cap for each map also plays a role in how your raids will feel. The “maxBotCap” settings can be found in the “raids.json” file within your settings folder. The larger the number of bots on the map the more the game cycles through spawning bot waves, however this is also the biggest contender in causing significant decrease in your game performance due to it having to render and calculate more bots. I recommend to have it set to be between 18-24 for larger maps and 10-16 for the smaller maps.

For example, say you are on Interchange and the “maxBotCap” value is 20. Once the game spawns in a total of 20 bots, any other bots after these 20 bots will not spawn until an existing bot(s) die and frees up a slot for other bot(s) to spawn in. This means bot spawn waves can be skipped if the “maxBotCap” is full. Evenly dispersing and offsetting the Scav and PMC spawns will keep them spawning/fighting consistently and prevent raids from becoming lifeless. This is why I like to try making the window of time that PMCs spawn to be a little offset from Scavs.

Lastly, I suggest using the Waypoints mod with BSP as it expands the size of these “openZones” making bots able to move more around the map.

comments.body_html:
Hey guys, found the brain error message you get with SAIN, just tested it in Factory against a PMC I found.

Go to the folder for the preset you have selected (I have the default LikeLiveTarkov selected) (user>mods>PreyToLive-BetterSpawnsPlus>config>settings_[PRESET]), then go to the bots.json file as a .txt file or however you would normally open a similar file if you have a 3rd party program for these type of things.

Inside of the bots.json file, 5 quotations down, there should be a “brainTypes” category; set it from “enabled”: true, -> “enabled”: false,

Don’t remove the commas, don’t capitalize things, just change the true to false. This allows the bots to still spawn as the rest of the mod intends without attempting to override bot brain types (thus causing SAIN errors).

Please lmk if this helps

comments.author: PreyToLive
comments.body_html:
Hey subspecies, glad you are enjoying the mod! I’ll try my best to answer your question.

All spawn waves/times/bot types/difficulties/etc for each map are predetermined before each raid based on the preset(s) that get chosen.

The “interval time” setting determines the spacing between spawns. So, for example if you have it set to 300 then at the end of every 5 minutes a new wave of bots will spawn in a random zone. This will last until the total pool of “waves” have spawned. (You can also add a slight time delay to each wave which just makes it so spawns don’t all spawn at the exact same time interval.)

Example:

Bot Type = Scavs

Bot Amount = [1,1,1,2]

Waves = 15

Interval Waves = 3

Interval Time = 500

Time Delay = 0

TIME: Raid Start —– 5mins —– 10mins —– 15mins —– 20mins —– 25mins —– Waves Stop

ZONE1: 0 Scavs —– 1 Scav —– 1 Scavs —— 1 Scav —— 1 Scav —–– 1 Scav —— No New Waves

ZONE2: 0 Scavs —– 2 Scav —– 1 Scavs —— 1 Scav —— 1 Scav —–– 2 Scav —— No New Waves

ZONE3: 0 Scavs —– 2 Scav —– 2 Scavs —— 1 Scav —— 2 Scav —–– 1 Scav —— No New Waves

The way the code picks a new “open zone” for each wave is sort of hard to explain but I’ll try.

The weight value of each “open zone” (0 is no chance and 4 is the highest chance) is what determines the spread of bots across the map. These weights are then thrown together into a pool and picked at random from it for each spawn wave. Once a zone is picked it is removed from the pool so it isn’t picked again. Once all are picked, the pool resets and starts the process again until all possible waves have a zone assigned to it. I came up with this method to ensure bots are dispersed evenly across the map. Increasing the weight for a zone will increase the amount of waves for that zone during a raid.

Example:

TOTAL WAVES: 8

ZONES WEIGHTS:

___ZONE1 = 0
___ZONE2 = 2
___ZONE3 = 1

___ZONE4 = 3

___ZONE5 = 0

ZONE POOL: [ ZONE2, ZONE2, ZONE3, ZONE4, ZONE4, ZONE4 ]

WAVE1 —– WAVE2 —– WAVE3 —– WAVE4 —– WAVE5 —– WAVE6 —|– WAVE7 —– WAVE8

ZONE4 —– ZONE3 —— ZONE2 —– ZONE4 —– ZONE4 —– ZONE2 —|– ZONE4 —– ZONE2
____________________________________________________Zone Pool Resets ^

Keep in mind each map has a Min/Max Bot Cap which is one of the other options you can find in the BSP mod. If the MaxBotCap is reached while in a raid then all spawn waves will be skipped until a bot dies in the raid and frees up a slot for another bot to spawn.

Hope that answers your question about when/how spawns are selected.

comments.author: metamorcat
comments.body_html:
Hi 3.9.8 lovers! yes im still playing on 3.9.8 cuz its the best version with the best selection of mods yes? i’ve found a potential bug in this mod, which causes the bosses spawn at the much delayed timings.

Bug Report: Boss spawn time doubled due to interval being added twice (v2.0.5)

Mod version: BetterSpawnsPlus v2.0.5 File: BSPClassLocations.ts, (line ~488)

Issue: When configuring a boss spawn wave with initial.time and a non-zero spawnDelay, the resulting spawn time is much delayed like double what it should be. If spawnDelay is set to 0, the resulting time is initial.time - 1 instead of exactly initial.time. I personally had set it initial.time=600, spawnDelay=60, but resulting the bosses were spawning at like 1200 secs during the raids.

Fix: Open BSPClassLocations.ts, and find the line 488, replace the line

randomTime = (randomTime === 0) ? -1 : Math.max(0, randomTime + timeInterval);

to

randomTime = (randomTime + timeInterval < 0) ? 0 : randomTime;
